reasons.clarity/compound-instruction: Audited 2026-09-12; line re-checked 2026-10-27. CLAUDE.md:147 is one bullet describing one hook (validate-rules-hook.py and the two validators it runs) in a list of hooks. The rule counted three verbs in a description and read it as a three-action directive.
reasons.clarity/escape-hatch-missing: Re-audited 2026-10-27 against the current entries. Every one is a deliberate unconditional rule, where an 'unless' clause would invite the exception the rule exists to refuse. Machine-gated, so no escape hatch exists to document: AGENTS.md:25 (stdlib-only shipped tools, check-stdlib-only.py), AGENTS.md:37 (command table 1:1 with command files, validate-skill.py), AGENTS.md:48 (version manifests in sync, mise run version-sync) and CLAUDE.md:82 (mise run check must pass, the gate itself). AGENTS.md:7 and :9 are the sub-agent-definition security boundary, where an escape hatch would be the defect. AGENTS.md:28 (internal scripts run through uv) and :41 (conventions live only in _conventions.md) are author discipline stated as absolutes on purpose.
reasons.clarity/undefined-term: Audited 2026-09-12; reason corrected after decompiling the rule. A bare /\b[A-Z]{2,5}\b/ match against a hardcoded allowlist, cleared when the term appears as 'TERM (' , 'TERM:' or '(TERM)' within a few lines. An earlier note here claimed expansion does not satisfy it; that is WRONG — verified that 'AST (Abstract Syntax Tree)' clears it. Re-audited 2026-10-27: the remaining entries are RED and GREEN at CLAUDE.md:79, a deliberate decline rather than an unsatisfiable rule. They are TDD phase names, defined in .claude/rules/skill-lifecycle.md:10 and by the skill-tester skill the same line points to. Editing prose to satisfy an ALL-CAPS pattern matcher, for terms the reader already knows, is the appeasement a baseline is supposed to make visible.
reasons.completeness/has-identity: Audited 2026-09-12; reason corrected after decompiling the rule. It reads no file contents: it passes if a file named SOUL.md or IDENTITY.md exists, or if CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md has any heading matching /identity|persona|who you are|character|personality|role/. Verified — a ZERO-BYTE SOUL.md clears it and lifts the score 96->97, and so does a heading '## Role of this repo'. So there is no design opinion here to accept or decline: satisfying it would change nothing about how any agent behaves, and would be a file added purely to move a linter's number. Not baselined because we disagree about personas — baselined because the check cannot distinguish an agent with an identity from one with an empty file.
reasons.consistency/outdated-cross-references: Re-audited 2026-10-27, each referent checked on disk. The remaining entries are AGENTS.md:44, :47 and :57, citing .claude/rules/vendored-skills.md, .claude/rules/commit-types.md and .claude/rules/snapshot-before-mutating.md. All three files exist at exactly the cited path; the rule reads a file path as a section heading.
reasons.runtime/config-exists: Audited 2026-09-12. N/A: the tool reporting its OWN skipped checks because no clawdbot.json / openclaw.json exists here. Not a statement about this repository, and there is nothing to fix — but it does mean agentlinter's runtime category is uncovered.
reasons.skill-safety/dangerous-commands: Audited 2026-09-12. commands/iac.md:41 names `curl \| sh` as a Dockerfile defect class to hunt for — backticked, and pipe-escaped for the markdown table — in the 'what to look for' column. That documentation example is the file's ONLY occurrence of the token; iac.md contains no executable pipe-to-shell command, and nothing it says is run (verified by grep). The rule matches the quoted text, not a command.
reasons.skill-safety/injection-vectors: Audited 2026-09-12, both in commands/prompt-safety.md — the command whose subject is prompt injection. Line 20 carries a quoted example payload inside the finding-format spec; line 27 is the table row defining the direct-prompt-injection class. Both are documentation of the pattern, not instructions addressed to a reading agent.
